issues.quote: It has run badly since he died, and I have never let anyone touch it.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives the watch readings (8:40 at dinner, 10:15, 10:18, 10:21, 10:32) as ordinary readings of Félix's watch. It says nothing about the watch being unreliable.
issues.misreading: A solver could reasonably conclude that the watch is unreliable, so none of its readings can be trusted to the minute and the timeline could be shifted. The transcript gives that doubt, which the sheet does not.

issues.quote: By then I was not counting anything.
issues.fact: The sheet says he counted the ten slow notes and did not count the quick high ones. It says nothing about whether he counted the doubled notes.
issues.misreading: This could be read as meaning he stopped counting during the doubled notes, which would make the count of the first group look like a partial or uncertain count.

issues.quote: He wanted to talk about the repeater, and what it would fetch, I think, though he did not say so in those words.
issues.fact: The sheet only says Girard came in at 10:32 and they sat together until eleven. It gives no purpose for the visit.
issues.misreading: A reader could take this as a motive or a hint about the reason Girard came, which the sheet does not give.
